claim_refuted: The SD-prenucleolus is population monotonic on convex games.
verdict: FALSE. Certified counterexample at n=3 (minimal possible size).

violating_pair.relation: S subset T, player 2 in both, T = S with player 0 added

interpretation: phi_2(v|S) = 1/2 > 1/3 = phi_2(v|T): adding player 0 to coalition {1,2} STRICTLY LOWERS player 2's SD-prenucleolus payoff, violating population monotonicity on a convex game.

certification.method: certified_sd_prenucleolus (float screen -> rational reconstruction -> exact SD-Kohlberg balanced-level-set certificate) on BOTH subgames; exact rational convexity check on the ambient game

significance: Separates the two monotonicities for the SD-prenucleolus on its home class: SD IS coalitionally monotonic on convex games (Arin-Katsev) but is NOT population monotonic there. Contrast: Dutta-Ray egalitarian solution IS population monotonic on convex games.
discovery_note: First found as an n=4 convex game (v=[0,0,0,0,0,2,0,2,0,0,0,0,4,6,4,6], pair {2,3} subset {0,2,3}, gap 1/3); the violation lived entirely in a convex 3-player subgame, so it reduces to this n=3 witness. n=3 is the minimum size for population monotonicity (needs |S|>=2, |T|>=3). Brute force over integer convex 3-player games confirms coalition-value sum 4, v(N)=2 is the smallest-magnitude form.
frequency_context: Float-screened PM violations occur in 206/400 (52%) of random convex games at n=4 and 140/200 (70%) at n=5 -- the failure is generic, not a rare edge case.
